title: hotfix: SLO enforcement and circuit breaker tweaks for regional failover & load-shedding under node pressure
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: A customer incident revealed a scenario where aggressive SLO enforcement plus circuit-breaker tripping on a subset of pods caused poor regional failover behavior and high error amplification during transient node pressure. This hotfix reduces amplification risk by adjusting enforcement backoff, prioritizing regional failover routing when capacity is constrained, and adding conservative load-shedding early in the pipeline.

What this PR does: 1) Adjust SLO enforcement backoff logic to use exponential backoff with capped jitter (reduces rapid re-trips). 2) Introduce an explicit regional_failover_priority flag that short-circuits local circuit-breaker fallback to avoid sending traffic to already overcommitted nodes in the same region. 3) Add a proactive load-shedding step (best-effort prefix/kvcache check) that rejects low-priority requests earlier when memory or queue depth exceeds threshold. 4) Emit new observability metrics (slo_enforce_backoff_count, regional_failover_attempts, shed_by_priority) and tags to allow correlation with incidents. 5) Add unit and integration tests and a small runtime GC safety check to avoid memory spikes during shedding.

Risk: Moderate. Changes are conservative defaults (regional_failover_priority=false by default in config) but the SLO backoff and load-shedding thresholds are enabled for Dedicated customers running release-2026-02 and for Hosted canary ring. The changes were validated in staging and a limited canary rollout.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge hotfix into main. 2) Deploy to canary pool for 2 hours with synthetic traffic and emergency rollback playbook available. 3) Gradual ramp to 10%/50%/100% over a day with close monitoring of shed_by_priority and error budget burn.

Related: Linear ENG-3421, ENG-3508. Jira: SUP-1189 (customer case).
